scenario.question: We move to combat and declare ALL TEN of our creatures as attackers against seat-2 (jarad-graveyard, 17 life): Zada, Hedron Grinder (3/3), Hanweir Garrison (2/3), General Kreat, the Boltbringer (2/2), five 1/1 Human Tokens and two 1/1 Goblin Tokens. We then activate Goblin Burrows once. seat-2 has TWO creatures — Reclamation Sage (2/1) untapped and Splinterfright (*/*) TAPPED. (a) Resolve every attack trigger in Comprehensive Rules order and state the total power attacking seat-2 and the non-combat damage dealt to it. (b) Is seat-2 dead before our end step, taking the most favourable block available to it? Cite the rule that decides whether Splinterfright can block.

steps.action: Precombat main phase ends and the BEGINNING OF COMBAT STEP begins. Its FIRST turn-based action chooses the DEFENDING PLAYER: this is a four-player Free-for-All, our three opponents do not all automatically become defending players (the Attack Multiple Players option is an option, not the default), so we choose one of them, and we choose seat-2 (jarad-graveyard, 17 life). That choice does not use the stack and it happens BEFORE any player receives priority. No ability on any of the four boards triggers at the beginning of combat; the active player (us) then receives priority, and this is the last window in which any opponent can act before attackers are declared.
steps.effect: The turn-based action is what makes seat-2 — rather than seat-3 or seat-4 — the defending player, and it is the premise of everything below; because 507.1 resolves before the priority round in 507.2, the defending player is locked in before the interaction window this step warns about, and no opponent can redirect the attack by acting in it. Then the triggers, enumerated rather than assumed: every permanent on all four boards was read for a 'beginning of combat' trigger and none has one — ours (Hanweir Garrison, Zada Hedron Grinder, General Kreat, Boggart Shenanigans, five Human Tokens, two Goblin Tokens, Goblin Burrows, three Mountains, Reliquary Tower, Fountainport), seat-2's (Ripples of Undeath, Lord of Extinction, Splinterfright, Reclamation Sage, three lands), seat-3's (two Talismans, Swiftfoot Boots, Abaddon the Despoiler, six lands) and seat-4's (Blind Obedience, Arcane Signet, Heliod Sun-Crowned, five lands). So nothing ON THE BOARD changes here. The step being empty of triggers is a finding, not a reason to skip it: we take no action and pass, and each opponent in turn order then gets priority with an untapped-land count and a hand we cannot see (seat-2: 0 untapped lands, 5 cards ESTIMATED; seat-3: 3 untapped lands, 0 cards; seat-4: 2 untapped lands, 3 cards). EVERYTHING BELOW IS CONTINGENT ON NO OPPONENT ACTING IN THIS WINDOW — a removal spell on Zada or General Kreat, or a fog, pre-empts the whole line before a single attacker is declared, and with the margin of 2 established in step 12 very little is needed.

citations.quote: if the game being played is a multiplayer game in which the active player’s opponents don’t all automatically become defending players, the active player chooses one of their opponents. That player becomes the defending player. This turn-based action doesn’t use the stack.
Second, the active player gets priority.
If a player has priority and chooses not to take any actions, that player passes.

steps.action: In the declare attackers step we declare all ten of our creatures as attackers against seat-2 (jarad-graveyard, 17 life — the defending player chosen by the turn-based action in step 1), and total their power: Zada, Hedron Grinder (3/3), Hanweir Garrison (2/3), General Kreat, the Boltbringer (2/2), five 1/1 Human Tokens and two 1/1 Goblin Tokens.
steps.effect: All ten are listed untapped on the board (scenario-facts `your_board.creature_bodies`, 10 bodies, nothing spent paying a cost), so the declaration is legal on the tap requirement. CAVEAT, stated rather than assumed: the lift does not reconstruct summoning sickness (`summoning_sick: null` on every body, and `extras.reconstruction_notes` says so), and the two Goblin Tokens are annotated 'created at the turn shown'. If either entered this turn without haste it could not legally have been declared; step 12 shows the verdict survives losing both. POWER TOTALLED: 3 (Zada) + 2 (Hanweir Garrison) + 2 (General Kreat) + 5x1 (Human Tokens) + 2x1 (Goblin Tokens) = 14 power declared as attacking seat-2. That is the figure that will become damage, since each attacker assigns damage equal to its power.

A creature can’t attack unless it has been under its controller’s control continuously since their most recent turn began.
Each attacking creature and each blocking creature assigns combat damage equal to its power.

steps.action: Identify every ability that triggers on this declaration and put them on the stack.
steps.effect: Two trigger. (i) Hanweir Garrison — 'Whenever this creature attacks, create two 1/1 red Human creature tokens that are tapped and attacking'; it was declared as an attacker, so it triggers. (ii) General Kreat, the Boltbringer — 'Whenever one or more Goblins you control attack, create a 1/1 red Goblin creature token that's tapped and attacking'. Goblins declared this attack, enumerated from type lines: Zada, Hedron Grinder (Legendary Creature - Goblin Ally), General Kreat (Legendary Creature - Goblin Soldier) and both Goblin Tokens. Hanweir Garrison is a Human Soldier and the five Human Tokens are Humans, so they do not feed this condition. The condition is 'one or more', a single trigger event, so it triggers exactly ONCE, not once per Goblin. Both abilities are ours, so we order them; the order is immaterial here. Nothing seat-2 controls triggers on being attacked.

They were never DECLARED as attackers, so they cause no further attack triggers (General Kreat's Goblin trigger does not re-fire, and they are Humans regardless). They are created during the DECLARE ATTACKERS step, so the rule that makes a creature put onto the battlefield attacking automatically unblocked does not apply — seat-2 may block them. Attacking power against seat-2 rises 14 -> 16.

steps.action: Declare blockers step: seat-2 chooses blockers. THIS IS THE RULE THE QUESTION ASKS FOR.
steps.effect: A chosen blocker must be UNTAPPED. seat-2's board carries three creatures: Reclamation Sage (2/1, UNTAPPED), Splinterfright (*/*, TAPPED) and Lord of Extinction (*/*, TAPPED). Splinterfright therefore CANNOT block, and neither can Lord of Extinction. Neither has vigilance in its oracle text (Splinterfright has trample only, which matters only when it attacks; Lord of Extinction has only its characteristic-defining ability), so the lift's caveat that 'vigilance is not visible in the log' cannot turn either of them into an available blocker. Nothing on any board grants blocking while tapped. So seat-2 has exactly ONE legal blocker, and it blocks exactly one attacking creature.

citations.quote: The chosen creatures must be untapped and they can’t also be battles. For each of the chosen creatures, the defending player chooses one creature for it to block

steps.action: THE CRUX: establish what Lord of Extinction actually is, and how far the artifact lets us go.
steps.effect: 'Lord of Extinction's power and toughness are each equal to the number of cards in all graveyards' is a characteristic-defining ability: it sets power and toughness from a stated condition, is recalculated continuously, and functions in every zone. The scenario cannot give us the number: `graveyard_is_a_floor: true` on every seat, because the lift derives graveyards from battlefield-death events only and the log emits no mill or discard zone events. What the artifact lists is 3 entries across all graveyards, and two of those (Abaddon the Despoiler, Sythis, Harvest's Hand) are commanders the same artifact places on the battlefield and in the command zone respectively, leaving Evolving Wilds as the only unambiguous graveyard card. The lists are demonstrably incomplete, and Splinterfright PROVES it: its own CDA sets its power and toughness to the number of creature cards in seat-2's graveyard, and the artifact lists seat-2's graveyard as EMPTY — at 0 it would be 0/0 and would already have been put into the graveyard as a state-based action. It is on the battlefield, so seat-2's graveyard holds at least one creature card. Derivable bound: Lord of Extinction is at least 1/1, and the true figure is far larger (seat-2 controls Ripples of Undeath, which mills three each of its controller's first main phases, and Splinterfright, which mills two each upkeep, on turn 27). WHICH WAY EACH FLOOR CUTS: a floor is a LOWER bound, so it supports only claims that get stronger as the value rises — 'it would kill anything of ours it blocked', 'we cannot expect to kill it in combat'. A floor on its TOUGHNESS may not be read as its toughness: 'it is only a 1/1, our attackers can kill it' is an over-claim the artifact does not license. Likewise a floor on its POWER may not be read as its power, so no claim that our creatures survive it is available. Neither bound is needed below.

citations.quote: Characteristic-defining abilities function in all zones.
The card may have a characteristic-defining ability that sets its power and/or toughness according to some stated condition.
If a creature has toughness 0 or less, it’s put into its owner’s graveyard.

steps.action: Resolve the block seat-2 would actually choose — the DEFENDER's most favourable option, enumerated rather than assumed.
steps.effect: Reclamation Sage is the only blocker and blocks one attacker. No attacker of ours has trample or any evasion ability (oracle text read for all four nontoken bodies and both token types: Hanweir Garrison, Zada, General Kreat and vanilla 1/1 tokens), so a blocked attacker assigns ALL its combat damage to the blocker and none to seat-2. The damage seat-2 can prevent therefore equals the power of whichever single attacker it blocks. Enumerated: Zada (3 power) prevents 3 — the maximum, since Zada is the largest attacker; Hanweir Garrison or General Kreat (2) prevents 2; any 1/1 token prevents 1, and if that token is a GOBLIN it dies to Zada-class damage... more precisely it dies to Reclamation Sage's 2 damage, which triggers Boggart Shenanigans ('Whenever another Goblin you control is put into a graveyard from the battlefield, you may have this enchantment deal 1 damage to target player') for 1 damage we aim at seat-2 — net 0 prevented. So seat-2's best block is Reclamation Sage on Zada, preventing 3. The MAXIMUM seat-2 can prevent by blocking is 3.

citations.quote: If exactly one creature is blocking it, it assigns all its combat damage to that creature.
An unblocked creature assigns its combat damage to the player, planeswalker, or battle it’s attacking.

steps.action: With blockers declared, we receive priority in the declare blockers step and activate Goblin Burrows once: '{1}{R}, {T}: Target Goblin creature gets +2/+0 until end of turn', targeting an UNBLOCKED Goblin (General Kreat, or either Goblin Token).
steps.effect: Goblin Burrows taps as part of its own cost, so it is available exactly once; {1}{R} comes from the untapped Mountains (scenario `mana.open` 6 untapped lands: Goblin Burrows, three Mountains, Reliquary Tower, Fountainport). Unblocked attacking power rises by 2. Holding the activation until after blocks is strictly better, but not load-bearing: activating it in the main phase instead lets seat-2 block the pumped creature, and the biggest thing it could then absorb is a pumped Zada at 5 — which, as step 12 shows, is still exactly lethal.

steps.action: Combat damage step: assign and deal all combat damage.
steps.effect: Total attacking power against seat-2 is 19: 14 declared + 1 (Hanweir Human token) + 1 (Hanweir Human token) + 1 (Kreat Goblin token) + 2 (Goblin Burrows). Zada is blocked and assigns its 3 to Reclamation Sage; every other attacker is unblocked and assigns to seat-2. COMBAT DAMAGE TO SEAT-2 = 19 - 3 = 16. Reclamation Sage simultaneously assigns its 2 to Zada. State-based actions then check: Reclamation Sage has 3 damage marked against toughness 1 and is destroyed; Zada (3/3) has 2 marked and survives. No Goblin WE control dies, so Boggart Shenanigans does not trigger in this line.

An unblocked creature assigns its combat damage to the player, planeswalker, or battle it’s attacking.
the total damage marked on it is greater than or equal to its toughness, that creature has been dealt lethal damage and is destroyed

steps.action: Verdict on (b): does seat-2 die before our end step?
steps.effect: YES, and it does not depend on Lord of Extinction at all. seat-2: 17 life - 3 non-combat (General Kreat's three enters triggers) - 16 combat = -2, and a player at 0 or less life loses the game as a state-based action — checked, per CR 704.3, whenever a player would next receive priority. What puts that check inside the COMBAT DAMAGE STEP is that step's own third item: once the damage of step 11 has been dealt, the active player gets priority while still in the combat damage step (510.3), and 704.3 makes the check happen then — in the combat damage step, not at end of turn. So seat-2 is dead well before our end step; nothing waits for it. Total damage delivered 19 against 17 life: MARGIN 2. Robustness, since the answer is close: seat-2 can prevent at most 3 by blocking (step 9) against a 6-point requirement, so no blocking choice saves it. If BOTH Goblin Tokens were summoning sick and could not legally attack (step 2's unreconstructed caveat), delivered damage falls to 17 — exactly lethal, seat-2 at 0, still dead. If we had pumped before blocks and seat-2 blocked a 5-power Zada, delivered is 17 — again exactly lethal. Losing any 3 further points of damage would save it, so the margin is real but thin. TWO LIMITS ON THIS RESULT. (1) SCOPE OF THE BOARD, RECOUNTED: this is the zada-v1 BRANCH list, and Hanweir Garrison is NOT in the current 99 (scenario-facts card_membership.NOT_IN_THE_DECK). Deleting the card deletes its OUTPUT as well, which iteration 1 got wrong by keeping the tokens: Hanweir Garrison — 'Whenever this creature attacks, create two 1/1 red Human creature tokens that are tapped and attacking' — is the ONLY source of Human tokens in either list. Set enumerated rather than asserted: every entry of the 99 and of the zada-v1 branch decklist read against data/cards.csv; the only other cards that mention Humans at all are Moggcatcher, Kessig Flamebreather and Firebrand Archer, each a Human itself and none of them a token maker, and no opponent's permanent makes Humans either. So all FIVE Human Tokens on this board trace to Hanweir Garrison and go with it. Derived independently, and it agrees with the checker's recount: the sleeved deck presents FOUR bodies — Zada (3), General Kreat (2) and two 1/1 Goblin Tokens — for 7 declared power; Kreat's Goblin-attack trigger still fires exactly once for one 1/1 Goblin token tapped and attacking (7 -> 8), that single enters event fires Kreat's second ability once for 1 damage to EACH opponent (1 to seat-2, pod total 3, not 3 per seat), and Goblin Burrows still pumps an unblocked Goblin (8 -> 10 attacking power). Reclamation Sage's best block is still Zada and still prevents 3, so combat damage to seat-2 is 10 - 3 = 7 — each attacking creature assigning combat damage equal to its power is what converts that attacking power into damage, in the counterfactual exactly as in step 11. 7 combat + 1 non-combat = 8 against 17 life: a SHORTFALL OF 9, not the 4 iteration 1 claimed — roughly double. (Five Human Tokens is an odd number and Hanweir makes them two at a time, so at least one earlier token is already missing from the lift or was lost; that cuts the same way, since the counterfactual removes all of them regardless.) The verdict is unchanged — it does not kill — but it is not close: this kill is NOT a line the sleeved goblin-storm deck can run. (2) NO INTERACTION is assumed, as the question poses it: seat-2 has 0 untapped lands and 5 cards in hand (an ESTIMATE per the lift), seat-3 has 3 untapped lands and 0 cards, seat-4 has 2 untapped lands and 3 cards. A free effect from any of the three could still change the arithmetic, and with a margin of 2 very little would be needed.

the game checks for any of the listed conditions for state-based actions, then performs all applicable state-based actions simultaneously as a single event
Third, the active player gets priority.

final_state.summary: It kills. Ten declared attackers (14 power) become 17 attacking power once Hanweir Garrison's two 1/1 Human tokens and General Kreat's 1/1 Goblin token are created tapped and attacking, and 19 after one Goblin Burrows activation held until after blocks. Those three tokens entering also fire General Kreat's second ability three times for 1 damage to EACH opponent: 3 per seat (pod total 9), taking seat-2 from 17 to 14. The crux collapses on one rule: seat-2's Lord of Extinction and Splinterfright are both TAPPED and CR 509.1a requires a blocker to be untapped, so the re-lifted Lord of Extinction cannot block and its characteristic-defining power/toughness never enters the arithmetic. Its size is not computable here anyway — the graveyard lists are a FLOOR (battlefield deaths only), and Splinterfright's presence on the battlefield proves seat-2's listed empty graveyard is wrong, giving only 'at least 1/1'. seat-2's only legal blocker is Reclamation Sage (2/1), which can prevent at most 3 (blocking Zada) against a 6-point requirement. 3 non-combat + 16 combat = 19 against 17 life: seat-2 at -2, dead by CR 704.5a, margin 2. The verdict survives both Goblin Tokens being summoning sick (exactly lethal at 0) and the worse pump sequencing (also exactly lethal). NOT a line the current deck can run: Hanweir Garrison is outside the 99, and it is the only source of Human tokens in either list, so removing it removes all five Human Tokens with it — the sleeved deck attacks with four bodies for 10 attacking power and delivers 7 combat + 1 non-combat = 8 against 17, a shortfall of 9.
